trace.reasoning: The patient presents with dizziness and lightheadedness, a classic symptom of bradycardia. The ECG shows a regular rhythm at 60 bpm with no P waves preceding the QRS complexes, indicating a complete absence of atrial activity. This specific pattern of no P waves and no QRS complexes is the hallmark of Third-degree (complete) AV block. While the notes mention a conflicting diagnosis of seizure, the clinical context of dizziness and the specific ECG findings of a regular rhythm without P waves strongly support Third-degree AV block over seizure or other causes. The absence of P waves rules out Sinus bradycardia, and the regularity rules out Mobitz types.

final_choices.A: Mobitz type I second-degree AV block
final_choices.C: Mobitz type II second-degree AV block
